title: Lanes, Passing & Merging
summary: Which lane to use, how to change lanes and check blind spots, when passing is legal and safe, and how to merge and be passed.

items: On a two-lane, two-way road, drive on the right side unless you are passing.
Stay centered in your lane.
On a road with two or more lanes your way, the far-left lane is mainly for passing.
If you are slower than most traffic, use the right lane. If many cars are passing you on the right, move over.
On a long highway trip with no plans to pass, stay out of the far-left lane.
If a faster driver comes up behind you in the left lane, move right when it is safe and let them pass.

blocks.text: Blind spots are areas beside and just behind your car, on both sides, that your mirrors do not show. Even correctly adjusted mirrors leave them, so you must turn your head.

items: Signal, even if you do not see anyone nearby.
Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you are moving: left shoulder for a move left, right shoulder for a move right.
Move smoothly when the lane is clear. If the head check shows a car in your blind spot, stay in your lane until it is clear.
A blind-spot monitor helps, but it can miss things. Still look over your shoulder.
On a road with three lanes your way, check that a driver in the far lane is not moving into the same middle lane.
Do not change lanes in the middle of an intersection.
Do not ride beside another car's rear corner, which is its blind spot. Speed up or drop back so the driver can see you.
Double solid yellow center lines: no passing from either direction.
Solid yellow on your side: you may not pass. Broken yellow on your side: you may pass when it is safe.
If you are passing and a no-passing zone starts just ahead, you must be back in your lane before it begins.
Never pass a vehicle that has slowed and signaled a left turn by going around its left side.
Do not use a center two-way left-turn lane to pass. It is only for turning.

blocks.text: A few states allow you to cross a solid yellow line in limited cases, such as to pass a bicyclist or a very slow vehicle when the way is clear. These exceptions vary; check your State Cheat Sheet.
Even with a broken line on your side, do not pass unless you can see far enough ahead to finish safely.

items: Near the top of a hill or on a curve, where you cannot see oncoming traffic.
At or near railroad crossings, intersections, narrow bridges, tunnels and underpasses. Stay behind until you are well past them.
Near driveways and side roads, where a vehicle could pull out into your path.
At night, when it is hard to judge how fast and how far away oncoming cars are.
When you would have to speed to get by. Most states do not let you exceed the speed limit while passing; a few allow a small margin on two-lane roads. Check your State Cheat Sheet.
When passing two vehicles at once, unless you have a clear view and room to return ahead of both.

blocks.text: An oncoming car far ahead may be closer and faster than it looks. If you start to pass and the other car speeds up or an oncoming car appears, slow down and pull back into your lane behind it.

items: Check that the road ahead is clear and passing is allowed.
Signal left, check your mirrors and left blind spot, then move left.
Pass on the left, on your side of the center line if the road has two lanes in each direction.
Signal right. Return only when you can see both headlights of the car you passed in your rearview mirror.
Do not cut back in too soon, or the driver you passed may have to brake hard.

blocks.text: You normally pass on the left. Passing on the right is generally allowed only when it is safe and either there are two or more lanes going your way (including one-way streets), or the car ahead is turning left and there is room on the pavement to get by.

items: Passing a left-turner on the right at an intersection: watch for oncoming left-turners and for pedestrians and bicyclists on the right.
Never pass on the shoulder or off the pavement, whether the shoulder is paved or not. Other drivers do not expect you there. If there is no room on the road, wait behind the turning car.
Stay in your lane and do not speed up. Speeding up can trap the passing driver in the oncoming lane.
On a road with no lane markings, keep as far right as is safe.

If you are driving well below the speed of traffic and a line builds up behind you on a two-lane road, pull over in a safe spot or turnout and let them pass. Some states require this once a set number of vehicles are behind you; check your State Cheat Sheet.
Double broken yellow lines on both sides usually mark a reversible lane. Before entering, check the signs or signals showing which way it is open.
A green arrow pointing down over a lane means you may use it. A red X means do not drive in it.
White diamonds mark a restricted lane, such as an HOV (carpool) lane.
An HOV lane is for vehicles with at least the posted number of people. HOV 2+ means at least two people, including the driver.
The required number of people and the hours the rules apply are posted on signs along the road.
If your lane is ending, signal, adjust your speed and merge into a safe gap. You must yield.
If you are in the through lane, adjust your speed to leave a gap for merging drivers.
In heavy, slow traffic, a zipper merge works best: drivers use both lanes up to the merge point and then take turns, one from each lane. Let the merging driver in.

keyPoints: Keep right except to pass; slower traffic uses the right lane.
Signal, check mirrors, then look over your shoulder before every lane change.
Mirrors and blind-spot monitors do not replace a head check.
No passing across a solid yellow line on your side, near hills, curves, intersections, railroad crossings, bridges or tunnels.
Pass on the left; pass on the right only where there are two or more lanes your way or a car is turning left, and never on the shoulder, paved or not.
Return after passing only when you see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.
When being passed, stay in your lane and do not speed up.
When a lane ends, the merging driver yields; in slow traffic, take turns like a zipper.
